LESSON: OBSERVING AND ARTICULATING SIGNS (LISTENING AND SPEAKING) 2.1.1 LISTENING AND OBSERVING FOR ENJOYMENT

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: MYSELF Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experienc
Topic 2.1: Observing and Articulating signs (listening and speaking) 2.1.1 Listening and observing for enjoyment
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and Articulating signs (listening and speaking) 2.1.1 Listening and observing for enjoyment, part of MYSELF Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experienc in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: how different ways people respond to music/dance (tapping, nodding, shaking different body parts). 1. How do people respond to music?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and Articulating signs (listening and speaking) 2.1.1 Listening and observing for enjoyment together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: observation skills as learner keenly observes peers performing various body movements

in responding to music.

• Creativity and imagination:Exploration- imagination and originality as learner shows different ways people respond to

music/dance (tapping, nodding, shaking).

Values:
• Unity: Cooperation as the learner collaborates with others to dance as a group.

• Love: hospitability as the learner interacts with others in singing and dancing thus becoming closer and appreciating others’

abilities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
16

Health related issues awareness as the learner dances and exercises body muscles while appreciating what music can do to our

health.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The theme myself brings about awareness of God’s creation that is related to Religious Education Activity areas.
